page: Microsoft Azure B32als_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine designed for workloads requiring variable CPU performance with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory configuration includes 64.0 GB of RAM, offering 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware virtualization is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, and the CPU feature set supports AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA instructions, while AVX-512 extensions are absent.

The instance does not include local ephemeral storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as Premium Storage. It operates without dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations place the B32als_v2 within the top 25 percent for single-core stress-ng performance (2702.69) and PassMark memory operations (2924.1). Multi-core processing aligns with median performance ranges, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 14441.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 39455.46. Memory throughput tests show 116.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 56.81 GB/sec for writes.

Cost efficiency is influenced by its burstable CPU allocation and low-memory design. While full compute capacity can be accessed during peak activity, sustained high CPU loads may be limited by credit accrual models. The configuration is well matched for bursty compute tasks, code compilation, build environments, static web serving, and development infrastructure that do not demand persistent full-core execution or large in-memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure B32als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine equipped with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture, it features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a compact 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote storage architectures. Benchmark data highlights strong single-core compute and memory metrics, placing in the upper quartile for stress-ng single-core processing and PassMark memory testing, while overall multi-core and compression workloads remain in the median tier. Because CPU capacity operates under a burstable credit profile, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for intermittent compute demands. It is technically suitable for compilation pipelines, dev-test environments, CI/CD runners, and variable traffic web servers.
